transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Foster (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (SE), Marcus Li (CSM) - Redwood; Aisha Khan, Tom Reyes, Elena Martin - Stormgate

Summary: quick intro, technical constraints, security checklist, plan pilot metrics and timeline, assign owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Foster: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie from Redwood, I'm the AE working with Stormgate on the pilot. How's everyone's day?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hey Jamie, thanks. Good yea, big day for us, trying to get the pilot lined up.
[00:12] Marcus Li: Hi all, Marcus on the success side. We'll run the onboarding cadence once Priya does the perf run.
[00:18] Tom Reyes: Tom here. We're mostly concerned about network and data residency stuff. Also a bit about cost tradeoffs.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Hi Tom, Priya, SE. I'll lead the baseline and give config recommendations - batching, KV cache hints.
[00:30] Elena Martin: Elena, security. We need SOC2 Type II evidence, SAML SSO integration, and KMS integration details.
[00:36] Jamie Foster: Great. Quick agenda — confirm pilot scope, security checklist, run perf on their typical 4k token prompts, then timeline and pricing. Anything to add?
[00:44] Aisha Khan: Add success metrics: latency targets and quality validation — we need to make sure responses don't regress versus our current LLM.
[00:50] Jamie Foster: Noted. Ok let's kick off scope. Aisha, can you describe the workload?
[00:56] Aisha Khan: Sure — it's primarily a customer support assistant, multi-turn, average session ~3-5 turns. Typical prompt context around 3k tokens, occasionally up to 4k. Throughput target initially small — 20-40 req/s for the pilot but single request p95 latency matters more.
[01:12] Priya Nair: Thanks, that helps. For 4k context we expect different kernels/quantization to matter. We'll run on Redwood Dedicated config and hosted to compare. I might mis-say product names but we'll be testing both hosted API and our Dedicated reserved pool.
[01:28] Tom Reyes: On network — we prefer VPC peering but need to confirm whether private control plane or customer-managed networking is required for our compliance posture.
[01:36] Jamie Foster: Right — Redwood Private offers VPC and on-prem options. For the pilot we can do VPC peering to the Dedicated pool; for higher compliance we have the Private deployment with customer-managed control plane.
[01:46] Elena Martin: Can you send the architecture diagram? We need to verify data flow and where logs go. Also audit logs retention.
[01:52] Marcus Li: We'll attach the runbook and the logging retention policy. Typically we can configure RBAC and audit log retention to meet enterprise needs.
[02:00] Aisha Khan: About data, some of our past transcripts contain PII. For pilot we will redact PII client-side, but we need to confirm at-rest encryption and HSM/KMS key usage.
[02:10] Priya Nair: We support integrations with customer KMS and HSM; keys can be managed by you. Also at-rest encryption is standard, we'll provide the KMS integration doc.
[02:18] Elena Martin: What's the default retention on logs? And can we disable storing raw payloads for pilot?
[02:24] Jamie Foster: Default retention is 90 days for debug traces, configurable. We can disable payload retention or anonymize at ingest for pilot. We'll share the security packet link in chat.
[02:34] Tom Reyes: Cool — send that. On perf, what are typical p95 numbers for 512 vs 4k on Dedicated?
[02:40] Priya Nair: For small context like 512 tokens p95 can be ~60–90ms depending on batch size, for 4k it jumps — expectation is 120–450ms p95 depending on model variant and quantization. We'll run exact numbers with your prompt set.
[02:56] Aisha Khan: That variance is big. Our SLO target is p95 <120ms for interactive flows. Is that realistic for 4k?
[03:04] Priya Nair: Maybe for optimized model variants and aggressive batching + KV cache reuse it can get closer, but for raw 4k end-to-end it's optimistic. We should set realistic pilot targets: maybe p95 <200ms and validate quality. We'll show tradeoffs.
[03:18] Jamie Foster: Right — cost is also a tradeoff. We'll show a pricing delta: hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved pool amortized. I'll produce a preliminary pricing note.
[03:28] Tom Reyes: For Dedicated, what's the minimum commit and burst options? We might need predictable throughput for peak support windows.
[03:34] Jamie Foster: Dedicated has monthly committed capacity; burst options are available for headroom. We'll include numbers in the pricing doc.
[03:40] Elena Martin: On SSO— we use SAML via Okta. Do you support SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[03:46] Marcus Li: Yes, SAML SSO & SCIM are supported. We'll share a SAML setup guide for admin team.
[03:52] Aisha Khan: For the pilot, what are acceptance criteria beyond latency? We want to include model quality checks (F1 on intent classification, hallucination rate <2%).
[03:58] Priya Nair: Good call — we'll run some eval sets against your prompt/response gold set. Can you share a small set (50–100 examples) to start?
[04:06] Aisha Khan: Yep, we'll share. We'll also include edge cases where context rolls off.
[04:12] Tom Reyes: On networking, we'll need a list of egress IPs if peering isn't possible. Also certs and mTLS?
[04:18] Jamie Foster: We can support VPC peering or IP allowlists. mTLS for service-to-service can be discussed with the infra team — it's supported in Private deployments.
[04:26] Elena Martin: Ok, please include a short note about logs going to our SIEM and retention.
[04:30] Marcus Li: Noted — we'll include the SIEM integration pattern and a suggested retention policy.
[04:36] Jamie Foster: Timeline - propose: baseline perf next week, run hosted vs dedicated comparison, security docs shared by Tues, pricing by Thurs, kickoff pilot the following week. Thoughts?
[04:44] Aisha Khan: That sounds good. We want the pilot to be two weeks long with a go/no-go at the end.
[04:50] Priya Nair: Two-week pilot is fine. For fairness we'll run a steady-state throughput test and some peak bursts.
[04:56] Tom Reyes: Can we schedule a bench run during off-hours to avoid hitting our prod stacks?
[05:00] Priya Nair: Absolutely, we can coordinate.
[05:04] Elena Martin: Any legal or PO needed before pilot?
[05:08] Jamie Foster: Usually for pilots we run on a standard pilot agreement; if you need a PO or specific DPA terms we'll surface. I'll have a template to share.
[05:16] Aisha Khan: Great. On data sovereignty — some users are EU-only. Does Redwood provide regional hosting?
[05:22] Jamie Foster: Yes, we have EU regions and options to pin models/requests to region. We'll note that in the security packet.
[05:28] Tom Reyes: Ok. A small nit — we've had issues with token accounting in past vendors; will you show token-level cost breakdown?
[05:34] Marcus Li: Yes, the console has token-level breakdowns and per-route cost analytics. We'll give access to a demo tenant.
[05:40] Aisha Khan: Cool. Any competitors we should be benchmarking against? We looked at Anthropic and Cerebras previously, and considered OpenAI for hosted.
[05:48] Priya Nair: We'll try to surface comparative metrics where possible, though vendor apples-to-apples can be tricky.
[05:54] Jamie Foster: Alright let's go into the perf baseline plan — Priya, can you outline the steps?
[05:58] Priya Nair: Sure: 1) collect a 50–100 prompt sample and a handful of multi-turn sessions; 2) run hosted API baseline to establish latency & token cost; 3) run Dedicated pool with recommended quantization/batching; 4) run quality evals against gold set; 5) deliver a short report with CSVs and suggested config. Each run will include raw csv of latencies and a summary.
[06:22] Aisha Khan: We'll upload the sample to the secure share link you provide.
[06:26] Jamie Foster: I'll put the drive link in the follow-up. Marcus will schedule the perf window.
[06:30] Tom Reyes: One more — does Redwood expose tracing hooks for per-request debugging?
[06:34] Priya Nair: Yes, short-lived debug traces and model-level logs. We can only share raw payloads based on your retention settings.
[06:40] Elena Martin: We'll want to see what PII redaction looks like in practice. Can you do a demo anonymization run?
[06:46] Marcus Li: We can run a quick demo as part of the baseline, show how payload can be redacted or hashed prior to storage.
[06:52] Jamie Foster: Ok wrapping up — quick recap of owners and dates. Priya runs perf baseline (due 2026-02-12), Marcus sends runbook and schedules weekly checkins (due 2026-02-07), Jamie sends pricing and pilot agreement template (due 2026-02-09), customer to share sample prompts and network diagram (due 2026-02-10).
[07:16] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Thank you all.
[07:18] Jamie Foster: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and calendar invites.
[07:22] (crosstalk) Tom Reyes: Thanks. Bye.

Post-meeting notes: Links shared in chat - security packet (link), onboarding runbook (link), sample pricing sheet (link). Transcript includes small mis-hearings; final artifacts will be attached to CRM.
